claims.claim: Nicolas Jimenez is out as CEO of BC Ferries and a review has been launched.
claims.episode_span: Nicolas Jimenez is out as chief executive of BC Ferries, and the board has launched a review.
claims.source_title: Nicolas Jimenez out as B.C. Ferries CEO, review launched
claims.supporting_quote: Nicolas Jimenez out as B.C. Ferries CEO, review launched

claims.claim: Brian Anderson was appointed interim CEO of BC Ferries effective immediately, and Dallyn Willis will lead a service review.
claims.episode_span: Brian Anderson, vice-president of strategy and planning, is interim CEO effective immediately.
claims.source_title: Hullo Ferries hires European transportation executive as its new CEO
claims.supporting_quote: Today, BC Ferries announced the sudden departure of CEO Nicolas Jimenez and appointed Brian Anderson, its vice-president of strategy and planning, as interim CEO effective immediately.

claims.claim: Jimenez took over at BC Ferries in 2023 after leaving ICBC, where he worked with then-Attorney General David Eby on no-fault insurance.
claims.episode_span: Jimenez took over in 2023 after leaving ICBC, where he had worked closely with then-Attorney General David Eby on the transition to no-fault insurance.
claims.source_title: Nicolas Jimenez out as B.C. Ferries CEO, review launched
claims.supporting_quote: Jimenez took over at B.C. Ferries in 2023 after leaving ICBC where he had worked closely with then-Attorney General David Eby on the transition to no-fault insurance.

claims.claim: Elections BC preliminary figures show 48 percent turnout, about 10 points below 2024.
claims.episode_span: Elections BC’s preliminary figures show 48 percent of eligible voters cast a ballot
claims.source_title: B.C. election sets record for lowest voter turnout
claims.supporting_quote: According to Elections BC, preliminary figures show just 48 per cent of eligible voters participated, down about 10 percentage points from the 2024 provincial election.

claims.claim: The NDP received more than 270,000 fewer votes than in 2024, and the Conservatives about 49,000 fewer.
claims.episode_span: The NDP received more than 270,000 fewer votes than in 2024.
claims.source_title: B.C. election sets record for lowest voter turnout
claims.supporting_quote: The NDP saw more than 270,000 fewer votes than it did in the 2024 election, a significant drop that suggests many of its previous supporters didn’t show up at the polls. By comparison, the Conservatives received about 49,000 fewer votes.

claims.claim: Saanich voted 68 percent against amalgamation with Victoria, while Victoria voted 62 percent in favour.
claims.episode_span: In Saanich, 24,663 votes, 68 percent, were against, and 11,626, 32 percent, were in favour.
claims.source_title: Victoria backs amalgamation, but Saanich voters reject becoming a single larger city with B.C.'s capital
claims.supporting_quote: According to the official results, Saanich recorded 24,663 votes against amalgamation, representing 68 per cent, compared with 11,626 votes in favour or 32 per cent.

claims.claim: Uniqlo will open a flagship in the former Nordstrom space at Pacific Centre early next year.
claims.episode_span: Uniqlo said it will open a flagship in the former Nordstrom building at Pacific Centre early next year
claims.source_title: Uniqlo to move into old Nordstrom building in downtown Vancouver
claims.supporting_quote: Japanese clothing store, Uniqlo , announced it is opening up a new flagship store early next year.

claims.claim: Richmond council unanimously renewed a heritage-boat program for two years with more than $320,000.
claims.episode_span: More than $320,000 is going into the project.
claims.source_title: Richmond Japanese Canadian heritage boats get new lease on life
claims.supporting_quote: The outgoing city council voted unanimously in favour of renewing the program another two years. Over $320,000 is being injected into the project, which will restore the boats for display at the Britannia Shipyards National Historic site in Steveston.

claims.claim: Doerkson said an independent fiscal review will be ordered next month and report in the new year.
claims.episode_span: Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson said an independent review of B.C.’s fiscal position will be ordered next month and will report in the new year
claims.source_title: Les Leyne: Second comeback for Conservatives came with big assist from Eby
claims.supporting_quote: He said an independent review will be ordered next month into B.C.’s fiscal position.

claims.claim: A B.C. man was fined $7,500 for possessing endangered northern abalone, banned from harvest since 1990.
claims.episode_span: A B.C. man has been fined $7,500 after being caught in possession of endangered northern abalone.
claims.source_title: B.C. man handed $7,500 fine for possessing endangered northern abalone
claims.supporting_quote: A British Columbia man has been fined $7,500 after being caught in the possession of endangered northern abalone — a kind of mollusk that's been covered by a harvesting ban since 1990.

claims.claim: YVR handled 2.815 million passengers in August 2026, its first month above 2.8 million.
claims.episode_span: Daily Hive, using YVR’s latest official statistics, put the August total at 2.815 million.
claims.source_title: Vancouver International Airport records its busiest month ever with over 2.8 million passengers
claims.supporting_quote: Canada’s second busiest airport recorded 2.815 million passengers in August 2026, topping the record of 2.73 million set in July 2026 by about 83,000 passengers.

claims.claim: Grand Chief Stewart Phillip called ripping up DRIPA a declaration of war, while Lorne Doerkson said the party will repeal it.
claims.episode_span: He said the chiefs will not stand idly by if the government-elect rips it up, and he called that “a declaration of war.”
claims.source_title: B.C. First Nations chief warns ripping up DRIPA is a ‘declaration of war’
